raw_text:
Here’s a focused 3-week reconditioning block to safely restore capacity, rebuild muscle and work capacity, and set him up to resume heavier training. It respects post-illness fatigue, uses conservative loading with rapid-but-safe progression, and emphasizes sleep, nutrition, and fatigue monitoring.

Overview
- Frequency: 4 days/week (Upper/Lower split + full-body accessory day). Optional light GPP on rest days.
- Intensity: Start ~60–70% of pre-illness estimated 1RMs with RIR-based autoregulation to manage fatigue.
- Goal metrics: Restore benchmarks to ~90–95% by Week 3 and set up a return to normal programming in Week 4.
- Warm-up every session: 5–8 min easy cardio + dynamic mobility (T-spine, hips, ankles, shoulders) + ramp-up sets for first lift.
- RPE/RIR guide: Target 2–3 RIR on main lifts Week 1; 1–2 RIR by Week 3.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec) on compounds first two weeks to reinforce technique and keep load in check.
- Conditioning: Low-to-moderate aerobic base work to aid recovery.

Key safety/monitoring
- Daily check-in: resting HR, perceived fatigue, sleep hours, soreness. If resting HR >10 bpm above baseline, cut session volume by ~25–40% or switch to low-intensity aerobic/mobility.
- If any return of illness symptoms (fever, chest tightness, unusual breathlessness), pause training and reassess.

Loading anchors (use as estimates; autoregulate by RIR)
- Pre-illness 1RMs: Bench 100, Squat 140, Deadlift 170.
- Week 1 start: 60–65% 1RM; Week 2: 70–75%; Week 3: 75–85% peaks for singles/doubles only if RIR target met and recovery markers good.

Week 1: Reintroduce volume and movement quality (RIR 2–3 on compounds)
Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench Press: 4 x 5 @ ~60–65% (2–3 RIR). 2–3 ramp-up sets.
- One-arm DB Row: 3 x 10–12, moderate, pause at top.
- Incline DB Bench: 3 x 8–10.
- Lat Pulldown or Weighted Pull-up (as capable): 3 x 6–8 (leave 2 RIR).
- DB Lateral Raise: 3 x 12–15.
- Face Pulls or Band Pull-aparts: 2–3 x 15–20.
- Optional finisher: easy Assault bike 6–8 min Z2.

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back Squat: 4 x 5 @ ~60–65% (2–3 RIR).
- RDL: 3 x 6–8, light-moderate (keep hamstrings fresh).
- Split Squat (rear foot elevated if comfortable): 3 x 8/side.
- Leg Curl: 3 x 10–12.
- Core: Side Plank 3 x 30–45s/side.
- 10 min Z2 bike or incline walk.

Day 3 – Upper B (pressing volume + scapular/rotator work)
- Close-Grip Bench or Neutral Grip DB Press: 3 x 6–8 @ ~60–65%.
- Seated Cable Row: 3 x 8–10.
- Overhead Press (barbell or DB): 3 x 5–6 light-moderate, 2–3 RIR.
- Chest-supported Rear Delt Fly: 3 x 12–15.
- Biceps Curl superset Triceps Pressdown: 2–3 x 10–12 each.
- Breathing cooldown: 3–5 min nasal breathing, 90/90 position.

Day 4 – Lower B + DL pattern
- Deadlift: 4 x 3 @ ~60–65% (keep bar speed crisp, 2–3 RIR).
- Pause Front Squat (2-sec pause): 3 x 3–4 light-moderate (technique).
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3 x 8–10.
- Calf Raise: 3 x 12–15.
- Core: Dead Bug 3 x 8–10/side.

Optional GPP (1–2x this week on rest days)
- 20–30 min Z2 cardio (bike/row/walk).
- Mobility: hips/T-spine/ankles 10 min.

Week 2: Progressive overload, restore strength endurance (RIR 1–2)
- Increase loads ~5–10% on compounds if Week 1 moved fast and recovery is good. Keep technique tight. Slightly reduce reps on heaviest sets where needed.

Day 1 – Upper A
- Bench Press: 1 x 5 @ 70–72.5%, then 3 x 4 @ same or +2.5% (1–2 RIR).
- One-arm DB Row: 4 x 8–10 (last set 1–2 RIR).
- Incline DB Bench: 3 x 6–8.
- Pull-ups or Pulldown: 4 x 5–6 (add small load if 5 reps easy).
- Lateral Raise: 3 x 12–15.
- Face Pulls: 2–3 x 15.

Day 2 – Lower A
- Back Squat: 1 x 5 @ 70–72.5%, then 3 x 4 @ same or +2.5% (1–2 RIR).
- RDL: 3 x 6–8 slightly heavier than Week 1.
- Split Squat: 3 x 8/side heavier or slower tempo.
- Leg Curl: 3 x 8–10 heavier.
- Core: Pallof Press 3 x 10/side.
- 8–12 min Z2 cardio.

Day 3 – Upper B
- Close-Grip Bench or DB Press: 3 x 5–6 @ ~70%.
- Seated Row: 4 x 6–8.
- Overhead Press: 3 x 4–5 @ ~65–70%.
- Rear Delt Fly: 3 x 12–15.
- Curls superset Pressdowns: 3 x 8–10 each.

Day 4 – Lower B + DL pattern
- Deadlift: 1 x 3 @ 70–72.5%, then 3 x 2–3 @ same (1–2 RIR).
- Front Squat (no pause): 3 x 3–5 light-moderate.
- Hip Thrust: 3 x 6–8 heavier.
- Calf Raise: 3 x 10–12.
- Core: Copenhagen Side Plank 3 x 20–30s/side.

Optional conditioning
- 1–2 sessions, 25–30 min Z2. If recovery solid, add 4–6 x 20-sec strides on a bike/rower with 1:40 easy between (keep HR sub-threshold).

Week 3: Reclaim neural drive; cautiously touch heavier intensities (RIR 1 most sets; zero RIR only on optional single if bar speed is great)
- Target exposures to 75–85% in low reps to prepare for normal training next week.

Day 1 – Upper A (bench focus)
- Bench Press: Ramp to a single at ~80–85% if warm-ups are fast and RIR ≥1; then 3 x 3 @ 72.5–77.5%.
- DB Row: 4 x 6–8 heavier.
- Incline DB Bench: 3 x 5–6.
- Weighted Pull-up or Pulldown: 4 x 4–6.
- Lateral Raise: 2–3 x 12–15.
- Triceps Pressdown: 2 x 10–12.

Day 2 – Lower A (squat focus)
- Back Squat: Ramp to a single at ~80–85% if criteria met; then 3 x 3 @ 72.5–77.5%.
- RDL: 3 x 5–6.
- Split Squat: 3 x 6–8/side.
- Leg Curl: 3 x 8–10.
- Core: Weighted Plank 3 x 30–45s.

Day 3 – Upper B
- Close-Grip Bench or OHP (choose one to push slightly):
  - If Close-Grip Bench: 3 x 3–4 @ 72.5–77.5%.
  - If OHP: 4 x 3 @ ~70–75%.
- Row variation: 3 x 6–8.
- Rear Delt Fly: 3 x 12–15.
- Arms superset: 2–3 x 8–10 each.

Day 4 – Lower B (deadlift focus)
- Deadlift: Ramp to a single at ~80–85% if criteria met; then 3 x 2–3 @ 72.5–77.5%.
- Front Squat: 3 x 3 light-moderate for positions.
- Hip Thrust: 3 x 5–6.
- Calf Raise: 3 x 10–12.
- Core: Hanging Knee Raise 3 x 8–12.

Criteria to attempt the heavier single (~80–85%)
- Resting HR near baseline, no unusual fatigue, warm-ups feel snappy, bar speed consistent, no form breakdown. If not met, skip the single and do straight sets in the 72.5–77.5% range.

Warm-up and ramping guidance (each main lift)
- Example bench ramp Week 3: bar x 15, 40 x 5, 60 x 3, 70 x 2, 77.5 x 1 (assess), optional 80–85% x 1, then back-off sets.
- Keep total warm-up exposures but avoid excessive fatigue.

Recovery and fatigue management
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night. If <7 hours, reduce session volume by 1–2 sets on accessories.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add 500–1000 ml on training days.
- Stress: 5–10 min daily low-intensity walks and diaphragmatic breathing.

Nutrition (aim: regain 4 kg gradually, support recovery)
- Caloric target: Start ~200–300 kcal above estimated maintenance Week 1; increase to +300–400 kcal Week 2–3 if bodyweight not trending +0.25–0.5 kg/week.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day, distribute over 4–5 meals. Include 30–40 g high-quality protein within 1–2 hours post-training.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day Week 1–2; 4–6 g/kg/day Week 3 (prioritize around training).
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day, adjust based on total calories.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day.
- Omega-3: 1–2 g EPA/DHA combined per day if dietary intake low.
- Electrolytes: Add sodium pre-session if sweat rate high; consider 1–2 cups low-cal electrolyte drink during longer sessions.

Conditioning specifics
- Z2 guidance: conversational pace, HR ~60–70% max. Keep it easy—purpose is recovery, not fatigue.
- Avoid high-impact intervals until Week 3 and keep them submaximal as programmed.

Return-to-normal readiness at end of Week 3
- Target benchmarks by feel and bar speed:
  - Bench: triples moving well in mid-70s%, optional single ~80–85% smooth.
  - Squat: same as above.
  - Deadlift: same; expect deadlift to lag slightly in feel—normal post-illness.
- If all criteria met, progress to regular strength training in Week 4 with top sets around 80–85% and normal volume. If not, hold an additional week at Week 3 structure before pushing intensity.

Notes for you as the trainer
- Use RIR to tailor daily: if he reports unusual fatigue, drop 1–2 sets from accessories and keep compounds at the low end of the prescribed %.
- Keep sessions under ~75 minutes initially.
- Encourage light daily movement and sunlight exposure to speed recovery.
